newsitem.title: GERMANY: Colt plans fibre optic network in Munich.
newsitem.headline: Colt plans fibre optic network in Munich.

text.p: Business phone company Colt Telecom GmbH said on Tuesday it planned to build a 100 million mark ($61.6 million) fibre optic network to provide corporate phone services in Munich.

Colt, which has already built a telecom network in Frankfurt, would also look to build similar fibre optic systems in Hamburg and Berlin this year, the subsidiary of Britain's Colt Telecom Group Plc said in a statement.
The Munich system would begin operation next autumn with 50 kms of cable in the centre of Munich, offering voice, data and video transmission services to businesses.
The firm did not say when it would begin building the Hamburg and Berlin systems.

"Munich is an extremely interesting business location with numerous companies in banking, media and high technology," said Horst Enzelmuller, Colt's managing director in Germany. "Many of our customers in Frankfurt have already enquired about services in Munich."
German electronics firm Siemens AG, which will supply the cable for the Munich ring, had also agreed to become a customer, Colt said.

In December Colt was one of three groups to win licenses from Germany's Post and Telecommunications Ministry to provide a public voice telephone service, breaking the last monopoly held by Deutsche Telekom AG.
-- Neal Boudette, Bonn Newsroom, +49-228 26097150 ($ = 1.623 German Marks)
